tip_en: For ح the friction is deep in the throat, not at the lips. Say a tired 'ahh' and tighten the pharynx.
هـ is a light breath from the open glottis. If you hear friction like clearing your throat, you said ح instead.
Hold the constriction of ح through the vowel that follows it; do not let it relax into هـ at the end of the word.
Think of fogging a mirror very softly: that is هـ. ح needs visible effort in the throat.

For ص pull the tongue body back and hollow the mouth; the sound is darker and heavier than س.
س is a front hiss near the teeth. In ص the tongue retreats and the resonance moves to the back of the mouth.
Keep the emphasis of ص through the whole syllable - it colours the neighbouring vowels.
If ص sounds like a plain س, the tongue tip is too far forward. Retract it and lower the jaw slightly.
